industry.why: Neutral. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): regulated, leveraged, long-duration assets are hit by his discount-rate line, offset by defensive demand; Ports lead at A but that is leadership only. Relative strength C now, C prior. No tilt.

sector.why: Underweight, carried; the special topic 'The Sector Memo on telecoms relative strength: pullback or structurally impaired?' ties this row to the same yield leg as the telecoms rows (the US ten-year under 4.5% would favour both), and nothing read this week moves the ten-year from the 5% last read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, F prior. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). One live holding, Helios Towers, now 7.21% and the largest position (from 5.17%), Thematic Fit/Momentum D through this row and Bottom-up B on its own case; the row is a blunt instrument on it and component 5 says so. Counter-case: contracted, inflation-linked revenue is the visible cash the regime pays for, and towers rally hardest when rates peak. Back to C on the ten-year under 4.5% or the Fed path marked down.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the Bank of England's decision of 5-Nov-26 is still unread and the headlines disagree on it (on hold according to MarketScreener, cutting in 2026 according to the Irish Examiner, both undated); a weaker November consumer confidence headline (Trading Economics, undated) was not confirmed as a print for the window. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book is 39% UK-listed by invested weight (component 5). Balanced on unread evidence, so Neutral is an absence here, not a judgement. To D on hawkish guidance when the decision is read; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

items.criterion: Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal at the 30-Oct month-end (Sector RS 41, Stock RS 70); on 10-Nov Sector RS 29, Stock RS 73.
Sector RS fell 41 to 29 since 30-Oct, its half present and deepening; Stock RS rose 66 to 73 since 4-Nov.
Stock RS four points lower at 30-Nov gives a sell signal, selling the whole holding when its replacement is bought, under your one-off in/out link.

items.criterion: Industry RS below 30, read each Friday

bullets.text: No sell signal at the Fri 6-Nov reading: Infrastructure's Industry RS is 46, 16 points above the line, in force to 13-Nov.
Down from 53 at 30-Oct, up from 33 four weeks ago; three steps of about 6.7 points (one industry place each) would take it to about 26, below 30.
It read below 30 every Friday from 7-Aug to 2-Oct, when the European towers lagged.

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: relative price is 13.2% below its 52W high on 10-Nov (21.3% at the 30-Oct month-end).
Moving away; 5.2% above its relative 200D MA, but 1.8% below its 13-Oct relative peak.
At a flat market a close at or below 198.4p on 30-Nov, 13.6% below 229.6p, gives a sell signal.

items.criterion: The 200D MA of relative price flat or falling over the month, read each Friday

bullets.text: No sell signal at the Fri 6-Nov reading: the relative 200D MA rose 1.59% over the month (1.54% on 10-Nov).
Slowing; at an unchanged relative price it bottoms at about +0.65% on Fri 18-Dec.
A 10% relative fall over two weeks brings the first flat reading to Fri 11-Dec; a 15% fall to Fri 4-Dec.

items.criterion: SS Sales or SS PT Net Upgrade Breadth below zero AND Stock RS below 50, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: at 30-Oct PT Net Upgrade Breadth was (17%) but Stock RS was 70; now revenue +71% and PT +57%.
Remote: Stock RS (73) would need to fall below 50 with analysts turning to cuts by 30-Nov.

items.criterion: A tranche 30% below its highest close since purchase, with Stock RS below 70

bullets.text: No sell signal: on the data file's dates every tranche's 30%-fall level is 160.72p, which is 30% below Tuesday's 229.6p close, itself a new highest close since purchase.
On your 15-May purchase date for tranche 1, its 30%-fall level is 171.63p (30% below the 245.19p close of 22-May), which is 25.3% below Tuesday's close.

adds.criterion: The rules: no sell signal from the six Sell Criteria

bullets.text: No Sell Criterion gives a sell signal at its reading, so the six Sell Criteria allow an add.
On the 10-Nov daily readings none gives a sell signal either; "Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70" is four Stock RS points away.
Stock RS below 70 at the 30-Nov month-end with Sector RS still below 50.

adds.criterion: The rules: room below the holding's limit

bullets.text: The limit blocks an add: Helios Towers is 7.50% of capital at current value against the 6.68% limit.
Limits govern purchases and never force a sale; the holding grew from 7.40% on 9-Nov with Tuesday's rise.
Room returns only if the holding's value falls below 6.68% of capital, or after a sale.

adds.criterion: Where Helios Towers stands for an add: pulling back or basing; may be retesting or forming a VCP; healthily retesting or breaking out

bullets.text: The second stage, may be retesting a rising MA, on the edge of the third: the close above 225.6p came on 0.95x volume, not 1.5x.
One stage above the Master Dashboard's first stage (Basing plausible, 3 of 4; Healthy Retest possible, 3 of 6); no volatility contraction pattern (0 of 4).
A close above 229.6p on 1.5x the 50D average makes it the third stage; a heavy-volume close below 225.6p returns it towards the first.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a positive retest of a rising MA

bullets.text: Present: the absolute 200D MA (+2.41% over 20 sessions) held at closes 0.7% to 1.0% above it, then the SP rose 12.5% in seven sessions.
Every trend-health MA test now passes (the 50D crossed above the 150D on 10-Nov); only the 52W high, 6.4% away, partly passes.
A heavy-volume fall back through the 20D MA (213.35p) would turn the retest into a failed rally.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a broadening of the case (momentum rising in guidance, sell-side estimates, technicals or peers)

bullets.text: Present in guidance and sell-side estimates: FY2026 tightened upward, 2027 above 3,000 additions, five of seven analysts raising revenue and EBITDA, none cutting.
Technicals partly (above every MA, highest close since 2-Jun, but on 0.95x volume); peers partly (Airtel Africa +10.5% from 30-Oct; European towers not upgrading).
Analysts cutting in their full post-results notes, or Airtel Africa breaking lower again.
On 4-Nov you wrote: "I added 1.57% to 7.0% at ~213p" and "We are now pretty much near full size at the ~7%"; nothing on Helios Towers since.
The limit agrees: at 7.50% of capital there is no room, so your view and the rules point the same way.
Nothing in the readings; a change of size is your decision.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
